data.narrative:
Furno Materials is a Seed-stage climate and energy technology company founded by Gurinder Nagra that has raised $11M to date. The broader Climate & Energy sector includes nine private peers and one public comparable (LNZA), with notable private companies including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen. However, the peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables to support a statistically robust peer-median valuation.

The stage-progression method is the primary applicable triangulation approach. Using the $11M total capital raised as a baseline valuation proxy and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical for progression from Seed to the next financing round yields an implied valuation of $28M. This method is well-grounded in observed venture capital markups between early-stage cohorts, though it assumes Furno will track median performance within its vintage and sector.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $23M (low) to $32M (high), with a median of $28M. This narrow range reflects reliance on a single methodology rather than methodological triangulation. Key uncertainties include the absence of near-peer benchmarks to validate stage-progression multiples specific to climate-tech, the company's actual product maturity and commercial traction relative to its $11M raised, and the prevailing cost-of-capital environment for follow-on rounds in the sector. A more granular valuation would benefit from additional same-stage or pre-revenue comparables within climate technology.
